problemText: Read this sentence from a story: 'The dog barked loudly when the mailman arrived at the gate.' Which part of this sentence is an EXPLICIT statement?
choices: The mailman felt scared by the dog's reaction because we must infer the mailman's emotions from context clues in the story.
The dog was protective of its owner's house based on what we can understand about the dog's behavior and purpose.
The dog barked loudly when the mailman arrived at the gate.
The dog had been trained to guard the property as shown by details we can figure out from the text.
hints: An explicit statement uses plain words that are written right there in the text.
Look for a fact you can point to word for word, with nothing to figure out.

problemText: Read this passage: 'Yuki had studied the spelling list every night for a week. On test day, she wrote each word carefully and checked her work twice before turning in her paper.' Which statement is an INFERENCE, not something the text states directly?
choices: Yuki studied the spelling list every night for a week.
The spelling test happened on a day Yuki had prepared for.
She checked her work twice before turning in her paper.
Yuki wanted to do well on the spelling test.
hints: An inference is something the text does not say in plain words but that you figure out from the details.
Look for a statement about what Yuki was thinking or feeling, not just what she did.

problemText:
A student read this passage and made the claim below. Is this claim an inference supported by textual evidence, or is it just restating something the text already says explicitly?

Passage: 'Kai arrived at soccer practice with his shin guards already on and his cleats laced tight.'

Student's claim: 'Kai arrived at soccer practice ready to play right away.'

Which is true?
choices: It is a valid inference because no sentence in the passage says Kai was ready to play.
It is just a restatement because the passage already says Kai had his shin guards on and cleats laced.
It is a guess because the passage does not explain why Kai wore his gear.
It is an assumption because being ready to play requires knowledge about soccer that the passage does not teach.
hints: Check whether any sentence in the passage uses the exact words 'ready to play.'
An inference combines details the text gives to reach a new conclusion; a restatement just rewrites what was already said.

problemText:
Read this passage, then decide which statement is a valid inference with proper textual evidence.

Passage: 'The library's new computer lab had been closed for three weeks. When it finally opened on Monday, there was a line of twenty students waiting at the door before the librarian unlocked it. By Wednesday, the computers were all taken up during lunch period, and a sign-up sheet had to be posted.'

Which inference below is best supported by evidence from the text?
choices: Students are not interested in using computers at school because they did not sign up for the scheduled time slots.
Students had been waiting to use the new computer lab and wanted to access it as soon as it became available.
The library ordered new computers because the old ones were broken and could no longer support student use.
The librarian decided to close the lab because too many students were using it at once and needed to manage access.
hints: Look for details showing student behavior and what those details suggest about student interest.
Point to the exact phrases that prove your answer: what did students do when the lab opened, and what does that tell you about how much they wanted it?

problemText:
A student read this passage and wrote an inference. Read both, then decide if the inference needs to be fixed because it includes information from outside the text.

Passage: 'Every afternoon at three o'clock, Mr. Chen locked his classroom door and walked to the gymnasium. He always carried a stack of clipboards and a whistle. The gymnasium was where students gathered for practice after school.'

Student's inference: 'Mr. Chen coaches a school sports team because he is athletic and loves to exercise.'

What should the student do to fix this inference?
choices: Change 'coaches' to 'works with' because the passage does not use the word coaches to describe Mr. Chen's role.
Remove the phrase 'a school sports team' because the passage never mentions a specific sport or team name.
Remove the phrase 'because he is athletic and loves to exercise' because those ideas come from outside the passage, not from its details.
Keep the entire inference but add supporting details about Mr. Chen's personality traits because the clipboard and whistle prove he must be someone who enjoys physical activity and fitness.
hints: An inference can only use details the passage itself provides; 'athletic' and 'loves to exercise' are not mentioned in the text.
Check whether the text actually says anything about why Mr. Chen does what he does, or whether the student added an outside belief.

problemText:
Read this passage, then answer the question that follows.

Passage: 'Jamila skipped her usual route through the park and took the long street instead. When she passed the old community center, she slowed down and stared at the colorful construction sign: NEW YOUTH CENTER OPENING NEXT MONTH. That evening, she spent two hours looking at the center's new website, clicked through every photo of the art studio, dance studio, and music room, and saved three pages of information in a folder.'

A reader makes this inference: 'Jamila is interested in the activities at the new youth center.' Which one of these is the BEST textual evidence to support that inference?
choices: Jamila took a long street instead of her usual route through the park, which shows she changed her normal behavior that day.
The construction sign said the center would open next month and displayed colorful information about the upcoming facility.
The youth center has an art studio, a dance studio, and a music room available for students to use.
She spent two hours looking at the website, clicked through every photo of the studios, and saved three pages of information.
hints: Look for the evidence that shows Jamila's own behavior and choices, not just facts about the building itself.
The strongest evidence shows what Jamila did with her time and attention, not just what exists at the center.

problemText: A story's plot moves through four stages in a specific order. Which stage comes immediately after the rising action?
choices: A new rising action
The exposition
The resolution
The climax
hints: Remember the order: exposition, rising action, climax, resolution.
The climax is the turning point where the outcome becomes decided.

problemText: Read this sentence: 'Maya had never tried out for the soccer team before, but this year she decided to give it a shot.' What plot stage does this sentence belong to, and why?
choices: Exposition, because it introduces the character and the ordinary situation before conflict appears
Rising action, because Maya is making an important decision that will lead to obstacles and complications in the plot
Climax, because trying out for the team represents the moment of greatest tension when Maya faces her biggest challenge
Resolution, because the decision has already been made and shows how Maya's conflict with herself has been settled
hints: Ask yourself: has any trouble or conflict shown up yet in this sentence?
Exposition sets up characters and situations before any problem appears.

problemText: A student is sorting a story and found this sentence: 'The skater fell during the final jump, but he managed to land on his feet and kept going.' At what plot stage is this sentence most likely to belong?
choices: Exposition, introducing the skater as a character
Rising action, showing a complication that builds tension
Climax, because falling is the most stressful moment
Resolution, showing how things turned out after the conflict
hints: The sentence shows something going wrong—a problem happening.
Does the outcome of the whole story turn at this moment, or is uncertainty still building?

problemText:
Read these four sentences from a story about two friends trying to build a treehouse.

1. 'Leo and Jamie had been planning their treehouse all summer long.'
2. 'They bought wood and nails, but the wood was warped, and when they hammered the first wall, it cracked straight down the middle.'
3. 'Leo suggested they reinforce it with extra supports, and Jamie test-drove the repair by climbing up halfway—and the wall held strong.'
4. 'By the end of the weekend, they had a solid treehouse and couldn't wait to invite other kids over.'

Which sentence is the climax?
choices: Sentence 1
Sentence 2
Sentence 3
Sentence 4
hints: The climax is where a decisive action or moment turns the outcome—the tension peaks and the question gets answered.
Look for the sentence where something actually HAPPENS to solve the problem, not just where the problem gets worse.

problemText: A student labeled a story's plot stages this way: the exposition introduces two friends who play chess every lunch period; the rising action happens when one friend forgets the chess set on the bus; the climax is when students gather around and ask if they can watch; and the resolution is when the friends find the chess set in the lost and found the next day. Which label is in the wrong stage?
choices: The exposition label is wrong
The rising action label is wrong
The resolution label is wrong
The climax label is wrong
hints: The climax is where the turning point happens—where something decisive occurs and the outcome becomes decided.
Ask yourself: does students gathering and asking to watch solve the problem of the lost chess set, or does it just show the problem getting worse?

problemText:
Read this partial story: 'Carmen had always wanted to write a comic book, so she spent three months drawing and writing pages in a sketchbook. She showed her work to her art teacher, who said it was good but needed better speech bubbles. Carmen redesigned every speech bubble to match comic book style, and her teacher entered it in a district art show. The comic book won third place in the show, and Carmen finally felt like a real artist.'

Which sentence marks the climax, and what makes it different from the sentence about the teacher's comment?
choices: The sentence about redesigning speech bubbles is the climax because that is where a decisive action solves the problem.
The teacher's comment is the climax because it is the first professional feedback Carmen receives.
The sentence about the teacher entering the work in the show is the climax because that event leads directly to the resolution.
The sentence about winning third place is the climax because that is the moment Carmen's goal is fully achieved.
hints: The climax is a turning point where the outcome actually turns—look for a decisive action or choice, not just an event that happens to the character.
The teacher's comment creates a new problem; the redesigned speech bubbles actually solve it and change the direction of the story.

problemText: Read this sentence from a story: 'When Jake heard the door slam, he froze and looked at his broken vase on the floor.' What is Jake's response to hearing the door slam?
choices: He freezes and looks at his broken vase
He is startled by loud noises
He feels guilty about breaking the vase
He is a careless person
hints: A response is what a character does, says, or thinks right after an event—look for actions or words in the text, not feelings you have to guess.
The event is the door slamming. What does Jake do or say immediately after? Use only the exact words the text provides.

problemText: Read the passage: 'During lunch, Amara's friend accidentally knocked her sandwich off the table. Amara bent down, picked it up, brushed off the crumbs, and took a bite without saying anything to her friend.' Which statement correctly describes how Amara responds to her friend knocking over her sandwich?
choices: Amara forgives her friend because she does not stay angry
Amara cleans up the sandwich and continues eating without complaint
Amara is annoyed but hides it well
Amara is a patient and forgiving person
hints: Focus on what Amara actually does—pick up the sandwich, brush it off, take a bite—not on what you think she might feel.
Avoid choosing a trait or feeling word that the text never uses. The response is shown through her actions, not told.

problemText: In a story, Chen's bicycle gets a flat tire on the way to practice. Which of the following best shows a response rather than just a claimed trait?
choices: Chen is the kind of person who never gives up and shows determination in all situations
Chen is determined and resourceful in the way he handles difficulties and obstacles
Chen pulls out his repair kit, finds the puncture, and patches it carefully
Chen demonstrates the trait of solving problems through his resourceful and persistent character
hints: A response is shown through actions or words you can find in the text, not through a sentence that assigns a label.
Look for what the character actually does, says, or thinks after the event, not a general description of who the character is.

problemText: Read this story: 'At the start of soccer season, Kenji stayed on the bench during scrimmages and told his coach he was not ready to play. Midway through the season, after the team's best striker got injured, Kenji had to play in a real game and scored two goals. Near the end of the season, Kenji volunteered to take penalty kicks and was the first player to sprint onto the field at the start of every match.' Which sentence best describes how Kenji changes from the beginning to the end?
choices: Kenji overcomes his initial hesitation about playing and gains confidence through practice and competition
Kenji learns from his experience on the bench during scrimmages and decides to work harder
Kenji becomes confident after his success in the injured striker's game
Kenji changes from staying off the field to eagerly taking on leadership roles like penalty kicks
hints: A change requires comparing how the character acts near the start with how the character acts near the end—not just describing one moment in the middle.
Look for evidence from both the beginning and the ending of the story. The starting point is avoiding play; the ending point is volunteering and sprinting onto the field.

problemText: A story includes this event: 'When Rae's group project partner did not show up to the presentation, Rae panicked and turned red, but she took a deep breath and presented the project alone.' Later in the same story, Rae misses one slide during a class discussion, laughs at herself, and keeps talking. Does this show that Rae has changed, or is it just two separate responses?
choices: It shows two separate responses because each event causes a reaction, but Rae is not shown doing things differently overall
It shows Rae has changed because she responded with different emotions in each situation, showing she learned from her first experience
It shows Rae has changed because she handles two separate challenges through her own efforts and remains composed through both events
It shows just responses, not a change, because the two moments involve different types of situations and different people reacting to them
hints: A change means the character is different at the end than at the start. Check whether the difference shows up later in the story, not just in the one sentence after the event.
To prove a change, find one detail from near the beginning and one from near the end that show the same kind of thing done in two different ways. Do both moments show Rae acting in a lasting new way?

problemText: A story states: 'Isaac is dependable and hardworking.' Later, the text shows: 'When his experiment failed and shattered glass covered the lab table, Isaac stared at it for thirty seconds, then left the room. For the rest of the week, he avoided the lab and did not turn in his next three assignments.' How does what the text actually shows about Isaac's behavior differ from the claim made at the start?
choices: The text shows Isaac is actually dependable because he takes time to think before acting
The claim says Isaac is hardworking, but his actions show him avoiding work and stopping his assignments
The text proves Isaac is dependable by showing he walks away calmly instead of breaking more things
There is no difference because staring and leaving are signs of someone who is hardworking
hints: A claimed trait is a sentence that assigns a quality in words, rather than one the character's actions show. Trust what the character does over what anyone says about them.
What does the claim say Isaac is? What do his actual actions—avoiding the lab and not turning in assignments—show instead? Are they the same or different?

problemText: In the lesson, you learned the difference between naming where a part sits in a story and naming what job that part does. Which of these is a description of a part's job in the overall structure?
choices: This sentence introduces a character's wish that will either be granted or denied by the end of the story.
This sentence sets up the broken bicycle lock that the ending depends on.
This sentence appears somewhere in the middle section of the text, between the opening and closing.
This sentence belongs to the second paragraph and describes what happens on a Tuesday afternoon.
hints: A job names what a part does for the rest of the story, not where it sits or what it says.
Look for an answer that points to a later moment in the story that needs this part.

problemText:
Read this story and answer the question below.

Sentence 1: Maya's parents told her that if she stayed calm during the thunderstorm, she could help her younger brother stay calm too.
Sentence 2: When lightning lit up Maya's room at midnight, she took slow, deep breaths and kept her voice quiet and steady.
Sentence 3: Her brother came to her door, trembling, but after ten minutes of sitting with Maya, he stopped shaking and fell asleep.

How does Sentence 2 fit into the overall structure of this story?
choices: It describes the specific moment when lightning strikes and shows what Maya physically does in response, establishing the behavior that leads to her brother's calming in Sentence 3.
It explains that the thunderstorm occurs at midnight and describes the darkness of Maya's room during the weather event.
It shows what Maya does when the lightning happens, so that her brother's calm reaction in Sentence 3 makes sense as a result of her behavior.
It tells us about Maya's personal characteristics, such as her ability to control her breathing and keep her voice steady when she is afraid.
hints: Ask what Sentence 3 needs from Sentence 2 to make sense.
The job is not just what happens in Sentence 2, but what later moment depends on it.

problemText:
Read this story and answer the question below.

Sentence 1: The old mailbox at the end of Kai's driveway had a rusty hinge that squeaked whenever anyone opened it.
Sentence 2: Kai's grandpa visited in July and oiled the hinge without being asked.
Sentence 3: In August, Kai's little cousin visited and was startled by an unfamiliar noise when the mailbox creaked open.
Sentence 4: Kai realized he had never heard that sound before and understood what his grandpa had done.

Which sentence is NOT describing a job that later parts of the story depend on?
choices: Sentence 1, because if it were cut out, Sentence 4 would make no sense.
Sentence 2, because without it, Sentence 3 would have no reason for the mailbox to be quiet.
Sentence 4, because it is the end of the story and nothing comes after it.
Sentence 3, because it only restates what happens without setting up anything later.
hints: Remember: a summary restates what happens in a part. A job points to a later moment that needs it.
Ask whether anything that happens after Sentence 3 would stop making sense if Sentence 3 were cut out.

problemText:
Read this story and answer the question below.

Sentence 1: The community garden plot that Taj's family adopted had crumbly, gray soil that wouldn't hold water.
Sentence 2: Over three months, Taj added mulch and compost every week, turning the soil rich and dark.
Sentence 3: When the tomato plants started growing, they grew twice as fast as the tomatoes in the plot next door.
Sentence 4: The neighboring gardener asked Taj what she had done differently, and Taj explained about the soil.
Sentence 5: By fall, three other families were working on their own soil the same way.

Explain the connection between Sentence 2 and Sentence 5. What is Sentence 2's job in the overall structure of this story?
choices: Sentence 2 sets up the rich soil that makes the tomatoes grow fast in Sentence 3, which leads the neighbor to ask Taj about her method in Sentence 4, and that exchange spreads the practice to three other families by Sentence 5.
Sentence 2 covers the three-month time period during which Taj performs weekly additions of mulch and compost to transform the soil into a darker and richer texture.
Sentence 2 demonstrates that compost and mulch improve soil quality, but Sentence 5 shows that other families learned this technique through their own experimentation rather than from Taj's example.
Sentence 2 proves that Taj is willing to work hard consistently over many weeks to improve her garden plot, which establishes her character as someone who perseveres.
hints: Trace the chain: which sentence needs the work from Sentence 2? Then, which sentence needs what happens in that one?
A complete job answer points to a payoff, but that payoff might not be the very next sentence.

problemText:
A student was asked how Sentence 1 fits into this story's overall structure, and answered: "Sentence 1 is at the beginning of the story." Explain what is wrong with that answer, and describe Sentence 1's actual job.

Sentence 1: Leo noticed that every time he tried to play his guitar in the living room, his dog Biscuit howled.
Sentence 2: The next day, Leo moved his guitar practice to the garage, where Biscuit couldn't hear him.
Sentence 3: A week later, Biscuit stopped howling whenever anyone turned on loud music anywhere in the house.
Sentence 4: Leo realized that by moving his practice away, he had accidentally broken his dog's habit of reacting to the sound.

Which statement best corrects the student's error and names Sentence 1's real job?
choices: The student was wrong because simply stating that a sentence appears first does not reveal what work that sentence does for the rest of the story; location and function are different things. The real job is that Sentence 1 introduces the howling behavior that Sentence 4 later explains was accidentally broken by Leo's decision to practice elsewhere.

Saying Sentence 1 is at the beginning only tells you where it sits, not what it does. The real job: Sentence 1 sets up the howling behavior that Sentence 4 explains as accidentally broken by Leo's absence.
Sentence 1 must be described by its sequence position rather than by what it accomplishes, because all sentences at the start of a story share the same structural purpose.
The student's answer was incomplete because it failed to identify the specific details about Leo's dog breed and the living room location that Sentence 1 provides as essential background.
hints: Location labels and structural jobs are two different things.
Ask what Sentence 4 needs from Sentence 1 to make sense.

problemText:
Read this story carefully, then answer the question below.

Sentence 1: In the spring, Mrs. Chen planted apple seeds in tiny pots on her kitchen windowsill, one for each student in the class.
Sentence 2: Over two months, the seedlings grew, and each student got a pot to take home and plant in their yard.
Sentence 3: By mid-June, some students sent photos of tall saplings with new leaves, while others' plants had turned brown and died.
Sentence 4: In the fall, Mrs. Chen asked the class to bring their plants back for a check-in day.
Sentence 5: Only half the saplings returned, and many had grown large and strong, while others were still struggling.
Sentence 6: Mrs. Chen told the class that caring for a living thing takes time and attention, and that different people learn this lesson at different speeds.

Sentence 1 serves a job for multiple later moments in this story. Which choice correctly identifies both of those jobs by pointing to the specific payoffs?
choices: Sentence 1 starts the story by introducing Mrs. Chen as a teacher and describes her action of planting seeds, which explains why there are plants available in Sentence 4.
Sentence 1 shows that Mrs. Chen is creative because she thought of an activity involving plants, but this does not connect to either the varying outcomes in Sentence 3 or the lesson in Sentence 6.

Sentence 1 sets up the planted seeds, which lead to the saplings in Sentence 3 that some students neglected and others nurtured. This contrast is what allows Sentence 6 to make its point about different people learning care at different speeds.

Sentence 1 establishes that there will be one plant per student, which makes Sentence 2's distribution possible and also ensures that Sentence 4's return day works as a measurement of how many plants survived.
hints: Trace what would stop making sense if Sentence 1 were cut. Would Sentence 3's contrast between healthy and dead plants still matter? Would Sentence 6's lesson?
A single sentence can set up material that pays off in more than one place, as long as you can point to each payoff.
